description: A director of employment legal must approve a resolution plan for a senior employee's retaliation and workplace-conduct dispute, including whether to mediate, investigation safeguards, the employee's return terms, insurance conditions, and mediator selection.

shared_context.S1: A senior product manager has alleged retaliation after raising workplace-conduct concerns and has threatened a civil claim and an administrative complaint.
shared_context.S2: The employee is currently on paid leave, and no resolution terms have been offered.
shared_context.S3: Dana Brooks has authority to approve the company's resolution plan and any settlement framework.
shared_context.S4: The firm's routine pre-resolution process is a short issue-spotting round in which employment, HR, insurance, and conflicts counsel each report any matter that could affect the proposed plan before Dana makes the final call.

PF1.text: While reviewing newly collected messages for the employee's threatened claim, Omar found a message in which the manager links the employee's reduced responsibilities to the employee's earlier complaint; the same review found that the manager deleted related messages after receiving a preservation notice. Omar has not circulated the supplemental finding because his draft litigation assessment is awaiting document-index reconciliation.

PF2.text: In a confidential HR check-in this week, the employee said the concrete conditions for returning are transfer to the Product Operations reporting line and a neutral employment reference; the employee did not identify a cash amount as a priority. Maya has not put this preference in the case summary because the employee asked that it remain within the resolution team.

PF3.text: The employment-practices liability policy covers a settlement of this claim only if the insurer gives written consent before execution and the agreement contains no admission of wrongdoing; Evelyn confirmed these conditions in the policy endorsement review but has not sent the confirmation to Dana because the broker is still attaching the endorsement schedule.

PF4.text: The proposed mediator, Elena Ruiz, represented the company's head of Product Operations in an unrelated employment investigation last year, creating a current organizational conflict for this dispute; Noah confirmed the conflict through the firm's engagement database and has not issued the ethics notice while the responsible-partner sign-off is pending.

acceptance_conditions: The plan must select mediation because the supplemental messages materially strengthen the retaliation risk.
An independent investigation must be required because the manager deleted messages after receiving a preservation notice.
The return arrangement must place the employee in the Product Operations reporting line.
The resolution must require a neutral employment reference.
Written insurer consent must be required before execution.
The agreement must contain no admission of wrongdoing.
The mediator must be Maya Chen rather than the conflicted proposed mediator Elena Ruiz.
The plan must include a commitment to preserve and reconcile the supplemental message collection.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'message_preservation' and c['target'] == 'supplemental_collection' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The newly found retaliation message changes the strategy from an ordinary resolution discussion to mediation, while the post-notice deletion changes the plan to require an independent investigation and preservation of the supplemental collection.
The employee's stated return conditions change the agreement from unspecified work-status terms to a Product Operations reporting line and a neutral reference.
The policy endorsement changes the execution conditions to written insurer consent and an agreement containing no admission of wrongdoing.
The confirmed organizational conflict changes the mediator selection from Elena Ruiz to the conflict-free alternative Maya Chen.
